## agent-ml-research
ML research experiment management tools

attachment.content:
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

Long-context language models place acute pressure on the key--value (KV) cache, which grows linearly with sequence length and dominates inference memory at scale \cite{kwon2023vllm, pope2023efficiently}.
Two complementary responses have emerged: \emph{attention head pruning}, which removes structurally redundant heads \cite{voita2019heads, michel2019sixteen}, and \emph{KV cache eviction}, which discards low-importance token positions from the cache \cite{snapkv-neurips2024, adakv-neurips2025}.
Deploying both simultaneously---\emph{compound sparsity}---is attractive because the compression gains multiply, but the resulting quality degradation can be super-additive: the joint loss exceeds the sum of individual losses \cite{spark-aaai2026, slim-icml2025}.

Prior work has characterized compound interaction as a property of the sparsity level---higher sparsity yields more interaction---but treats the interaction magnitude as roughly constant across the generation process \cite{spark-aaai2026, unicomp-2026}.
This assumption is problematic for reasoning-capable models, whose generations are structurally heterogeneous: a single chain-of-thought trace alternates between phases of broadly distributed attention (exploratory reasoning) and phases of sharply concentrated attention (structured computation) \cite{thinkv-iclr2026, decision-repr-transition-2026}.
If compound interaction severity varies across these phases, then a uniform sparsity budget---the standard deployment practice---may be safe in one phase yet destructive in another.

We investigate whether compound sparsity severity is modulated by reasoning phase and eviction strategy.
Our central finding is that it is, and strongly so: under importance-based KV cache eviction, the Interaction Index---a measure of super-additive compound degradation---is concentrated in the low-sparsity phase (where attention distributes broadly) and largely absent in the high-sparsity phase (where attention is focused).
This \emph{severity gradient} grows monotonically with the sparsity budget: on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, the median phase difference in Interaction Index rises from $0.39$ at $s{=}0.15$ to $14.59$ at $s{=}0.30$, with paired effect sizes increasing from $d{=}0.44$ (small) to $d{=}0.80$ (large); Bonferroni-corrected permutation tests confirm significance at all four sparsity levels on this model ($p < 0.005$).
The pattern replicates at $s \geq 0.20$ on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct ($d \geq 0.55$) with attenuated absolute magnitude, though the effect at $s{=}0.15$ is marginal ($d{=}0.28$, bootstrap CI includes zero).
Critically, random eviction produces no such gradient: 7/8 conditions across both models fail to exhibit a significant phase difference (the single exception---Qwen $s{=}0.30$---has negligible effect size, $d{=}{-}0.04$), confirming that the severity gradient is an emergent property of the interaction between importance scoring and phase-dependent attention structure, not an artifact of compound sparsity per se.

We propose \emph{entropy-discrimination collapse} as an explanatory mechanism.
Head pruning forces surviving heads to redistribute attention mass, increasing attention entropy.
In low-sparsity phases, where attention is already broadly distributed, this redistribution flattens the cumulative importance scores used for KV eviction, degrading their discriminative power.
Importance-based eviction then degenerates into a biased pseudo-random process that can inadvertently remove critical positions---amplifying compound severity.
In high-sparsity phases, attention concentration is preserved after pruning, importance scores remain discriminative, and eviction remains well-targeted.
Random eviction is immune to this mechanism because its decisions are independent of attention patterns.

Our contributions are as follows:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
    \item We identify a \textbf{phase--strategy interaction} in compound sparsity: importance-based eviction exhibits a severity gradient across reasoning phases that is absent under random eviction (\S\ref{sec:experiments}).
    \item We show that this severity gradient \textbf{increases monotonically with sparsity} and replicate the finding at moderate-to-high sparsity ($s \geq 0.20$) across two models with different training regimes (distillation vs.\ instruction tuning), establishing robustness within the Qwen2 architecture family (\S\ref{sec:experiments}).
    \item We propose \textbf{entropy-discrimination collapse} as a mechanistic explanation, linking head pruning to the degradation of importance-score discriminability in a phase-dependent manner (\S\ref{sec:analysis}).
\end{enumerate}

These findings challenge the implicit assumption that compound interaction magnitude is phase-invariant, and suggest that sparsity budgets should be allocated in a phase-aware manner---tightening compression during low-sparsity reasoning phases where compound interaction is most severe.
The remainder of this paper is organized as follows: \S\ref{sec:related} surveys related work on compound compression, KV cache eviction, and phase-aware inference; \S\ref{sec:background} formalizes compound sparsity and introduces the Interaction Index; \S\ref{sec:experimental-setup} describes our experimental setup; \S\ref{sec:experiments} presents the main results; \S\ref{sec:analysis} analyzes the entropy-discrimination collapse mechanism; and \S\ref{sec:discussion} discusses implications and limitations.

## 任务：在服务器上编译论文 + 初始化 git repo

### 目标
1. 在服务器 westd-22162 上搭建论文编译环境
2. 将本地 paper 文件同步到服务器
3. 编译论文生成 PDF
4. 初始化 git repo + 初始 commit

### 环境信息
- 服务器: westd-22162
- 论文源文件本地路径: `/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/phase-gated-compound-sparse/artifacts/_project/paper/`
- 服务器上已有图表: `/root/autodl-tmp/pacs/figures/` (fig1_dose_response.pdf, fig2_cohens_d.pdf, fig3_crossover.pdf, fig4_bootstrap.pdf, fig5_crossmodel.pdf, dose_response_6point.pdf, crossover_6point.pdf, cohens_d_6point.pdf 等)

### 步骤

**Step 1: 探测服务器环境**
用 ssh_read_only 检查：
```bash
which pdflatex && pdflatex --version | head -1
which bibtex && bibtex --version | head -1
which latexmk && latexmk --version | head -2
ls /root/autodl-tmp/pacs/figures/*.pdf 2>/dev/null | head -20
```
如果没有 pdflatex，用 ssh_execute 安装：`apt-get update && apt-get install -y texlive-latex-base texlive-latex-extra texlive-fonts-recommended texlive-bibtex-extra biber texlive-science`

**Step 2: 在服务器上创建论文工作目录**
```bash
mkdir -p /root/autodl-tmp/pacs/paper/figures
```

**Step 3: 读取本地文件并写入服务器**
用 Read 工具读取本地的每个 .tex 和 .bib 文件，然后用 ssh_execute 写入服务器 `/root/autodl-tmp/pacs/paper/`。

需要同步的文件（仅当前活跃的 section，跳过旧版 *_fc6d1d.tex, *_46fb53.tex, *_4cc5f3.tex, results_5_1.tex 等）：
- main.tex
- abstract.tex
- introduction.tex
- related_work.tex
- background.tex
- methodology.tex
- results.tex
- analysis.tex
- discussion.tex
- conclusion.tex
- references.bib

对每个文件：先 Read 本地路径，然后 ssh_execute `cat > /root/autodl-tmp/pacs/paper/FILENAME << 'TEXEOF'\n...\nTEXEOF`

**Step 4: 链接/复制图表**
```bash
# 复制已有图表到 paper/figures/ 目录
cp /root/autodl-tmp/pacs/figures/*.pdf /root/autodl-tmp/pacs/paper/figures/ 2>/dev/null
cp /root/autodl-tmp/pacs/figures/*.png /root/autodl-tmp/pacs/paper/figures/ 2>/dev/null
ls -la /root/autodl-tmp/pacs/paper/figures/
```

**Step 5: 编译**
```bash
cd /root/autodl-tmp/pacs/paper && pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode main.tex 2>&1 | tail -30
cd /root/autodl-tmp/pacs/paper && bibtex main 2>&1
cd /root/autodl-tmp/pacs/paper && pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode main.tex 2>&1 | tail -10
cd /root/autodl-tmp/pacs/paper && pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode main.tex 2>&1 | tail -10
```

如果编译报错，分析错误并修复。常见问题：
- Missing package → `apt-get install texlive-xxx`
- Undefined citation → 检查 bib key 拼写
- Missing figure → 检查 figures/ 目录
- acl_natbib.bst not found → 把 bibliographystyle 改为 plainnat 或下载 acl_natbib.bst

编译成功标准：生成 main.pdf，无 fatal error（warning 可接受）。

**Step 6: 验证 PDF**
```bash
ls -la /root/autodl-tmp/pacs/paper/main.pdf
# 检查页数
pdfinfo /root/autodl-tmp/pacs/paper/main.pdf 2>/dev/null || python3 -c "
import subprocess
result = subprocess.run(['pdftotext', '/root/autodl-tmp/pacs/paper/main.pdf', '-', '-l', '1'], capture_output=True, text=True)
print(result.stdout[:500])
"
```

**Step 7: 初始化 git repo**
```bash
cd /root/autodl-tmp/pacs/paper
git init
git add main.tex abstract.tex introduction.tex related_work.tex background.tex methodology.tex results.tex analysis.tex discussion.tex conclusion.tex references.bib
git add figures/*.pdf figures/*.png 2>/dev/null
git commit -m "Initial commit: full paper draft with bf16 data

All 9 sections complete (Abstract + §1-§8)
35 success experiments, cross-model replication
Cohen's d paired d_z values throughout
Figures: dose-response, crossover, bootstrap, cross-model"
```

**Step 8: 报告**
汇报：
- 编译是否成功（附错误/warning 摘要）
- PDF 页数和大小
- git repo 路径和 commit hash
- 遗留问题（如缺失的图表引用、未解决的 warning）

25	Our contributions are as follows:
26	\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
27	    \item We identify a \textbf{phase--strategy interaction} in compound sparsity: importance-based eviction exhibits a severity gradient across reasoning phases that is absent under random eviction (\S\ref{sec:experiments}).
28	    \item We show that this severity gradient \textbf{increases monotonically with sparsity} and replicate the finding at moderate-to-high sparsity ($s \geq 0.20$) across two models with different training regimes (distillation vs.\ instruction tuning), establishing robustness within the Qwen2 architecture family (\S\ref{sec:experiments}).
29	    \item We propose \textbf{entropy-discrimination collapse} as a mechanistic explanation, linking head pruning to the degradation of importance-score discriminability in a phase-dependent manner (\S\ref{sec:analysis}).
30	\end{enumerate}
31	
32	These findings challenge the implicit assumption that compound interaction magnitude is phase-invariant, and suggest that sparsity budgets should be allocated in a phase-aware manner---tightening compression during low-sparsity reasoning phases where compound interaction is most severe.
33	The remainder of this paper is organized as follows: \S\ref{sec:related} surveys related work on compound compression, KV cache eviction, and phase-aware inference; \S\ref{sec:background} formalizes compound sparsity and introduces the Interaction Index; \S\ref{sec:experimental-setup} describes our experimental setup; \S\ref{sec:experiments} presents the main results; \S\ref{sec:analysis} analyzes the entropy-discrimination collapse mechanism; and \S\ref{sec:discussion} discusses implications and limitations.

Our contributions are as follows:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
    \item We identify a \textbf{phase--strategy interaction} in compound sparsity: importance-based eviction exhibits a severity gradient across reasoning phases that is absent under random eviction (\S\ref{sec:experiments}).
    \item We show that this severity gradient \textbf{increases monotonically with sparsity} and replicate the finding at moderate-to-high sparsity ($s \geq 0.20$) across two models with different training regimes (distillation vs.\ instruction tuning), establishing robustness within the Qwen2 architecture family (\S\ref{sec:experiments}).
    \item We propose \textbf{entropy-discrimination collapse} as a mechanistic explanation, linking head pruning to the degradation of importance-score discriminability in a phase-dependent manner (\S\ref{sec:analysis}).
\end{enumerate}

These findings challenge the implicit assumption that compound interaction magnitude is phase-invariant, and suggest that sparsity budgets should be allocated in a phase-aware manner---tightening compression during low-sparsity reasoning phases where compound interaction is most severe.
The remainder of this paper is organized as follows: \S\ref{sec:related} surveys related work on compound compression, KV cache eviction, and phase-aware inference; \S\ref{sec:background} formalizes compound sparsity and introduces the Interaction Index; \S\ref{sec:experimental-setup} describes our experimental setup; \S\ref{sec:experiments} presents the main results; \S\ref{sec:analysis} analyzes the entropy-discrimination collapse mechanism; and \S\ref{sec:discussion} discusses implications and limitations.

A notable exception among the random baselines is the Qwen random condition at $s{=}0.30$, which yields a statistically significant result ($p{=}0.012$) despite negligible effect size ($d{=}{-}0.04$, bootstrap CI excluding zero). % exp_id: qw_rand_s030; B=10000, p=0.012, d=-0.035, negligible
This case illustrates that dichotomous significance testing can flag effects of no practical magnitude---reinforcing the importance of reporting effect sizes and confidence intervals alongside $p$-values.

\paragraph{Sparsity range.}
Our experiments span $s \in \{0.15, 0.20, 0.25, 0.30\}$, a moderate range representative of practical deployment targets.
More extreme sparsity ($s > 0.50$) may exhibit qualitatively different interaction dynamics---the sub-exponential growth pattern suggests the severity gradient may plateau, but this remains unverified.
